app.name: TidyDash
app.summary: For people who want one tidy place for small personal bits. Scattered notes, counts, to-dos and links are hard to keep together. TidyDash lets them create a dashboard, add note, counter, checklist and link-list widgets, then configure, arrange and use them with automatic saving.
app.audience: People building personal dashboards for notes, counts, tasks and links

roles.name: Member
roles.description: Builds and owns personal dashboards and widgets

vocabulary.description: Named container for widgets; has name and last edited time
Block inside a dashboard of type note, counter, checklist or link list; has title, position, size small/medium/large and type settings
Single to-do inside a checklist widget; has text and ticked or unticked state
Single entry inside a link list widget; has title and web address

capabilities.note: Email and password sign up, sign in, sign out for dashboard owners
Each user sees only their own dashboards and widgets
Create, list, rename, duplicate, delete dashboards; add, rename, configure, remove widgets and their items
Change widget position relative to other widgets; new widgets append at end
Show when each dashboard was last edited
Public landing page explaining personal dashboards and how to start

inScope: Public landing page that says what personal dashboards are for and how to start
Create dashboards; list shows all of my dashboards with when each was last edited
Rename, duplicate and delete dashboards; dashboards are private to their owner
Open a dashboard in an editor that saves changes automatically
Add note, counter, checklist and link list widgets and configure title plus type settings
Rename widget, change its position relative to other widgets, resize between small, medium and large, and remove it
Use widgets in place: edit note text, increase or decrease counter with label, tick off and add checklist items, add titles with web addresses and open links

assumptions.text: New dashboards start empty with the name Untitled dashboard which can be renamed immediately.
Duplicating a dashboard creates a full copy named Copy of {name} with copies of all its widgets and sets last edited to now.
Deleting a dashboard permanently removes it and all its widgets after a confirm, with no trash or undo; removing a widget permanently removes its items.
New widgets are appended at the end in medium size with sensible defaults: empty note text, counter 0 with empty label, empty checklist, empty link list.
Counter value starts at 0, increases or decreases by 1 per tap, allows negative values, with no min or max.
Checklist items have text and ticked state, start unticked, require text to add.
Link entries require a title and a web address; addresses starting without http(s) get https prepended and open in a new tab.
Dashboards and widgets are private to the user who created them; there is no sharing.
Any dashboard or widget change updates last edited to now and autosaves immediately with a saved indicator; refresh restores the saved state.
Widget order is a relative list order; exact on-screen placement is up to the design.

questions.question: Should there be limits on number of dashboards or widgets per dashboard?
questions.whyItMatters: Determines whether validation and limit messaging are in scope

questions.question: Should deleted dashboards or widgets be recoverable from trash?
questions.whyItMatters: Changes data retention and UI scope
questions.defaultAnswer: No, delete is permanent with confirm
